Reference hashes make source state explicit, snapshots preserve accepted point-in-time outputs, and approval SHA checks bind human decisions to concrete content evidence; the work is documentary and continuity-focused, not an implementation expansion.
Principle: Evidence is stronger than plausible continuity; if an input is unknown, mark it TBD rather than inferring a value.
Principle: A snapshot means preserved state; a snapshot-producing workflow creates a new timestamped folder and may move a pointer but must not overwrite a previously accepted snapshot.
Principle: Hash bypass is exceptional and human-approved; when used it needs human approval and a durable record, with HASH_VERIFICATION_BYPASS.jsonl as the deliverable-local record surface.
Principle: CHANGE/SHA checks are reliance controls; approval evidence must bind to specific content, normally a git SHA or equivalent immutable evidence, and changed content needs renewed review.
Principle: Runtime audit records do not approve project work; runtime logs explain what happened but do not substitute for accepted project-state files or human approval records.
Treat docs/PRD.md as accessible but warning-qualified because REF-006 is HASH_MISMATCH; prefer matching CONTRACT/SPEC/DIRECTIVE/TYPES sources where available.
Use approval, issue, sign, seal, certify, and validate only for human-controlled processes; do not attribute those actions to agents or tools.
_LATEST.md is mutable convenience metadata; the timestamped snapshot folder is the durable point-in-time artifact.
Requiring durable bypass records makes source exceptions auditable but adds review overhead when a hash mismatch is intentionally accepted.

When a source file hash differs from _REFERENCES.md, record the mismatch as a source-state warning, use the source only as instructed or corroborated, and require human/source-hash reconciliation before final acceptance.
When a workflow reruns snapshot generation, create a new timestamped snapshot folder and update _LATEST.md if the workflow owns that pointer; do not overwrite an accepted prior snapshot.
When CHANGE is asked to publish after edits, confirm approval token/SHA evidence, compare current candidate content to approved evidence, and recheck HEAD before approved actions.
